audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[].side read 'Skill' while content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Brand on all seven rows.
audit.why: Two layers agreed on Brand and only the full-layer side column dissented, so the page rendered two answers to who wins each stage.
Brand: level 3 E-Q package, level 6 Pyroclasm (100s), Liandry's. Lux: level 6 Final Spark at 60s falling to 40s, plus the Lost Chapter timing that fixes her mana on 70-110 cost Lucent Singularity.
audit.corrected: enemyWin now names the actual Q-E-R sequence and its ranges.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page was written as if Lux were a short-range trader — whys[1] literally says 'Lux's short-range trades'. Her Q is 1175, W 1150, E 1100 and R 3340; every one of them outranges Brand's 1050 Sear and 900 Pillar. The minion-block on Light Binding was asserted without the mechanism, and Illumination's auto-attack payoff was never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text: Light Binding binds up to two enemy units, so the first body it touches absorbs it. Illumination charges the target and only detonates on Lux's next basic attack — deny the auto and a third of her poke never lands.
audit.corrected: Stated the range gap, gave Light Binding's stop-on-first-target mechanism with its flat 10s, and put the Illumination auto payoff into whys[1].

audit.why: Light Binding is a flat 10s at every rank, Lucent Singularity 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, Final Spark 60/50/40s.

notes: All four packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES: 'Pillar of Flame' and 'Final Spark' are both the correct Riot names for Brand's W and Lux's R, and the near-miss distances are just case and possessive noise. No ability-name corrections were needed on this matchup. The autoReset flag on Illumination is loose — Riot's text describes an empowered next attack, not an attack-speed reset — so I wrote only what the description supports (her poke is incomplete until she lands the auto). Full-layer phases[].side read 'Skill' on all seven rows against Brand x7 in both the packet and content win[]; aligned. Paired win[N] edits included as unchanged pairs to keep the chart group atomic. Lux outranges Brand on Q, W, E and R and the page never said so — I fixed the worst offender (whys[1] calling her a short-range trader) and put the range gap into dontsFull[2].d, but breakdown.early and breakdown.mid still read as generic Brand text that could sit on any enemy.
